key_insight: A 3D COMSOL opto-electro-thermal model shows that an n-ZnSe/p-SrScCu3Se4/p+-WSe2 heterostructure can achieve high photovoltaic performance, with optimized efficiency reaching 29.217%.
engineering_relevance: The results identify SrScCu3Se4 as a promising absorber for high-efficiency, thermally aware thin-film solar-cell design and guide thickness, doping, and defect-control optimization.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and thermal loss
Parameter sweep on absorber width, acceptor density, and bulk defects
evidence_signal: Under optimized conditions, the device reached VOC = 1.02 V, JSC = 32.472 mA/cm2, FF = 88.212%, and PCE = 29.217%, with QE strongest in the visible range.
watch_item: Performance is inferred from simulation; practical fabrication tolerances, interface quality, and real defect distributions may reduce the predicted efficiency.
paper_title: Computational analysis and performance optimization of SrScCu3Se4-based solar cells using COMSOL Multiphysics
